task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a straight news update of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about Bramble Quay's new after-hours library tool-return service. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 4, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Bramble Quay Library Board approved after-hours tool-return lockers at four of its six branches on Sept. 3, 2026.
Each participating branch will have 16 compartments, giving the first installation 64 compartments across the library system.
The service is scheduled to begin Oct. 5, 2026; installation work has begun but the lockers are not yet available.
The library lends household tools such as drills and sewing machines, but those items currently must be returned to a staffed desk.
The approved $128,000 project budget covers installation and the first year of maintenance, financed by a designated foundation grant.
The library estimates annual maintenance after the first year at $12,000, which the grant does not cover; a future operating allocation is still needed.
Borrowers will reserve an appropriately sized compartment through their library account or ask a branch employee to reserve one.
A recorded deposit time will determine whether an item was returned before its deadline, even when staff inspect it the following day.
Depositing a tool will not immediately clear it from the account because an employee must check its parts and condition.
Library director Osa Merrin said in the announcement, "Returning something should not require taking time off work."
The lockers will accept returns only; borrowing a tool will still require the existing checkout process inside a branch.
Oversized equipment and items with leaking containers are excluded from the lockers and must be returned during staffed hours.
The two branches left out of the first installation lack a suitable space under their current building leases.
A tenants association near one excluded branch asked the board to publish options for residents who cannot travel to another branch.
Association secretary Devra Senn said, "An extra option across town is not the same option for someone carrying a sewing machine."
Borrowers may return a loan to any of the four equipped branches, regardless of where they borrowed the item.
The board has asked staff for a January 2027 review of compartment availability, incomplete returns and requests made through branch employees.
The review will not begin with a target for reducing staff positions, and the approved plan contains no staffing cuts.
Library staff will empty and check the compartments before each participating branch opens on its next staffed day.
The tool collection began with donated garden equipment, although the library now purchases replacement items through its regular collection budget.
Printed locker instructions will be available at all six branches, including the two that do not receive lockers.
The library has not yet collected usage data for the service or estimated how many borrowers will change their return habits.

forbidden_additions: An operating service at all six branches.
After-hours borrowing or instant clearance of a returned item.
Demonstrated usage, time savings or staff reductions.
preserve: Different consequences of deposit time and subsequent inspection.
The access concern at excluded branches and the available cross-branch return option.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
